A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same sequential mean-testing study. Their main text, equations, five figures, and Appendices A-C are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original Beta and Bernoulli simulations and DSSAT crop-yield bootstrap results, displayed in Figures 1-5.

after.justification: Section 5 retains the original simulations and DSSAT bootstrap results in Figures 1-5.

M1.justification: The empirical KLinf stopping rule in Equation (3), both evaluated boundary choices, and the plug-in interval construction remain unchanged. The revisions concern theoretical validity and exposition.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Beta(3,2), Bernoulli(0.6), and normalized DSSAT crop-yield settings. Appendix B discusses distribution families theoretically without adding experimental coverage.

E2.justification: Both versions use the same Gaussian reference distributions and compare the same two stopping-boundary choices. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Section 5 retains the sample sizes, null means, error levels, threshold functions, histogram binning, and DSSAT bootstrap procedures. No experimental setting is substantively revised.

E4.justification: The sample-size convergence illustrations and comparisons across error levels and stopping boundaries are retained. No ablation, robustness test, or supplementary empirical analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report 5,000 synthetic replications and 3,000 DSSAT bootstrap paths, with unchanged variance estimation and interval-reporting practices. The revised theoretical conditions for confidence-interval validity do not change the empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Figures 1-5 contain unchanged results, and Section 5 retains the same findings. The reported empirical intervals [6.0,50.0] and [22.0,84.0], and single-path intervals [2.0,41.0] and [11.9,49.0], are identical.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 replaces the uniform KLinf bound with max{log(1/mo), log(1/(1-mo))}. Appendix A.3 corrects the centered boundary inequalities and explicitly proves that the threshold corrections vanish at the CLT scale. v2 also handles Dirac distributions explicitly, restricts Proposition 4.5 to nondegenerate distributions, and adds Assumption 4.1 to supporting lemma statements. These are localized repairs within the retained theoretical framework.

C1.justification: Introduction contribution 3 narrows its description from a confidence interval for stopping time to one for the leading-order normalized stopping-time center. Proposition 4.5 already identified the target as 1/KLinf in v1, so this corrects the advertised scope while retaining the central CLT contributions.

C2.justification: v2 removes the informal characterization of Assumption 4.1 as excluding sufficiently heavy boundary mass and Appendix B's assertion that all results extend to arbitrary bounded intervals by rescaling. It also drops the description of DSSAT yields as having a nonparametric distributional shape. The principal finite-sample interpretations and bounded-support limitations remain.

D1.justification: The dual-optimization description, normalization and bootstrap information, and DSSAT access link are unchanged. No implementation, resource, code-access, or reproducibility information is added.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a paragraph distinguishing second-order error-exponent research under sample-size constraints from this paper's stopping-time fluctuations as alpha approaches zero. Both intended citations render as question marks, and the bibliography remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 revises setup notation and prose, clarifies the Section 4.2 heading, expands proof exposition, and corrects several typos and cross-references. The overall section and appendix organization is retained.

P2.justification: The same five figures retain their plotted content, axes, legends, and captions, but their placement changes; Figures 1 and 4 move between columns. Expanded equations also reflow the appendix layout. No figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: v2 improves mathematical reliability through the boundary-algebra correction in Appendix A.3, the corrected uniform bound, and the nondegeneracy restriction on Proposition 4.5. Its revised contribution statement also identifies the interval's target more accurately. These localized gains outweigh the unresolved citations introduced in Section 2; the empirical evidence remains unchanged.
